verdict_reason: MDM commodity-line migration is correct against the frontend rules (ostrich 01063300 carries no identifiers), but the add-a-line steps are copied three times beside the promoted helper, one title claims dogs it never tests, and one absence check could be positive.

todos.issue: All three tests (lines 13-22, 63-72, 90-99) inline the add-a-commodity-line sequence ('What are you importing?' -> searchAndCheckSpecies -> save -> 'Commodity details' -> count -> save) that this PR promoted to AnimalsJourney.addCommodityLine; the promoted helper hardcodes one line and a count of 1, so the copies here (count 2, and two lines at once) were left behind. Guide: promoting a helper deletes the local copies.
todos.fix: Must: these tests reach the identification task through one journey-flow method that takes the lines and the animal count, with no inline copy of the steps. One way: extend addCommodityLine to accept several lines and an { animalCount } option, and call it from each test.

todos.issue: Title 'a unit form shows only the identifier types the commodity requires, plus the permanent address for cats and dogs' claims dogs, but the test only adds a Felis catus line; no dog line is exercised (frontend PERMANENT_ADDRESS_SPECIES in services/commodities/rules.js also covers ferrets, so the list is incomplete as well as unproven).
todos.fix: Must: the title states only what the assertions prove: a domestic-cat line's unit form shows passport, tattoo and permanent address, hides ear tag and horse name, and refuses a partial address. One way: retitle to 'a domestic cat's unit form asks for passport, tattoo and a permanent address, and refuses a partial address'.

todos.issue: Line 78 proves the ostrich line gets no panel with an absence check (heading 'Enter details for Struthio' toHaveCount(0)); a panel titled any other way for the ostrich line would pass it. House rules: prove absence with an exact positive assertion where one is possible.
todos.fix: Must: the test asserts the exact set of identification panels the page renders, so an extra panel for the ostrich line fails it. One way: assert the page's level-2 'Enter details for ...' headings toHaveText with a one-item list holding the cattle line's 'Enter details for Bos taurus' heading (via a page-object accessor such as animalIdentification.panelHeadings).
